svg.aria-label: A cross-validation score is an estimate of future performance, and the only way to know whether it is right is to compare it against a holdout of unseen customers in future periods
svg.text: A CV SCORE IS AN ESTIMATE. OF WHAT?
On real data you never see the answer, so nobody checks. Here the answer is held back on purpose.
Deployment means two things at once, and a fold that respects only one is still wrong:
customers the model has never seen AND periods that had not happened yet
THE PANEL: 15,211 ROWS, 2,600 CUSTOMERS, 12 PERIODS
DEVELOPMENT
periods 0 to 8, 1,649 customers, 7,030 rows
Everything cross-validation is allowed to touch.
Every scheme in this project splits THIS, and only this.
The latent per-customer effect lives here too, which is why
a fold that reuses a customer is quietly reading the answer.
THE TRUTH HOLDOUT
periods 9 to 11, 571 customers, 1,507 rows
Unseen customers.
Future periods.
Touched exactly once, at the end.
No customer appears on both sides.
cv_auc = what the scheme claims
truth = what actually happens
optimism = cv_auc minus truth Positive means the scheme flattered the model.
